cohort: Women who delivered between January 2014 and June 2018 at a single tertiary care center
finding: Delayed-onset postpartum preeclampsia was associated with non-Hispanic black race, obesity, cesarean delivery, and an increased risk of chronic hypertension.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was significantly more likely in women with delayed-onset postpartum preeclampsia compared to controls (40.5% vs 25.8%, P<.01).
